title: Normalized diagram-site tensor shifts and action unitors
statement: For arbitrary natural-number ring sequence A with adjacent maps δ and any scheme W, use the ringed sequence site, fixed derived tensor and predicates of [def-pur-diagram-pullback-shift-data]. There is a TensorConstraints T at W for which TensorCoherence T holds: the normalized signed two-shift, associator and symmetry comparisons admit the representative-normalized action unitors and obey all the stated single-slot shift laws, simultaneous extraction, signed interchange, associativity, symmetry and unitor shift equations. No geometric pullback or compositor is asserted.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); more-algebra.tex item-shift-tensor and item-flip-tensor-product. Parent proof steps 1, 4, 5 and tensor portion of 6.

proof.text: Take the uniquely normalized derived shift, associator and symmetry maps. The degree-zero ring is resolving because tensor with it is the identity; localize its chain action unitors and extend from resolving inputs, obtaining the two model normalizations.

On resolving inputs use the signed total-tensor equations. Single-slot zero and addition laws are the bifunctor shift laws; extracting second then first gives extraction and the two orders differ by (-1)^(ab). The associator exponents bp+c(p+q) and cq+(b+c)p agree; symmetry exponents differ by 2bp. The degree-zero ring factor makes both unitor exponents zero.
Insert the canonical representative comparisons and extend these chain equalities uniquely to all derived inputs by faithful restriction in each finite tuple.
